parole.significato: a shepherd that operates a hut for his flock
parole.testo: Unknown and disputed. Possibly of an eastern, but pre-Turkish origin (e.g. Cuman, other Turkic, or perhaps Iranian). Has cognates in each of the languages surrounding Romania. Also found in Aromanian as baci. May alternatively be a native, pre-Roman substrate word. Possibly from Albanian bac.
Unknown. Either a substrate word or derived expressively from bob (“type of bean”).

parole.significato: A net fixed to a circular frame for catching small fish. alternative form of chepcel

parole.testo: A local substrate of unknown relation to Ancient Greek θύμβρα (thúmbra) and Proto-Slavic *čębьrъ, *čǫbьrъ.

Formerly ‘bastard’, compare with Albanian kopil, Byzantine Greek κοπέλα (kopéla). Alternatively an old ultimately paleo-Balkan substrate word. Compare Aromanian cochil, Megleno-Romanian copil (“bastard”), cupilaș (“child”).
Unknown. Probably a substrate word. Compare Albanian molikë.

parole.significato: mamaliga, cornmeal mush, polenta (a porridge-like dish made of coarse maize-meal)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Possibly a substrate word or an expressive creation based on mamă or Latin mamilla (representing the idea of nourishment) + -ică. Alternately, it can be inherited from Latin [Term?], akin to Italian meliga (“maize, sorghum”), from Latin milium (“millet”).
Possibly a substrate word. Alternatively, it may be ultimately linked to Ancient Greek μάραθον (márathon, “fennel”), but is not a direct derivation. Compare Albanian mërajë.

Uncertain; possibly an expressive formation (variant of pop; cf. also coc), or a substrate term (compare Albanian pupë (“bud”)), or less likely linked to (Vulgar) Latin puppa (“teat, nipple”). More likely ultimately from Proto-Slavic *pǫpъ (compare Serbo-Croatian pup (“bud”)) or Hungarian pup, altho

parole.testo: Definite origin uncertain. Possibly a substrate word, akin to Albanian rosë (< *ratsa?), or from South Slavic (compare Serbo-Croatian and Slovene raca, Serbian dialect race, Bulgarian ряца (rjaca)); compare also Friulian raze, Occitan rit, Hungarian réce, Romani ratsoy.
Possibly from a pre-Roman substrate language, likely Slavic. Compare Old Church Slavonic рокъ (rokŭ), from Proto-Slavic *rokъ.
